Lower Bounds for the Weisfeiler–Leman Algorithm via Implicit Parity Systems

      Abstract

      The kkk-dimensional Weisfeiler–Leman algorithm (kkk-WL) is a simple combinatorial algorithm that was originally designed as a heuristic for the graph isomorphism problem, but which also has surprising connections to areas such as logic, homomorphism counts, linear programming, proof complexity, (symmetric) algebraic complexity, and machine learning. This submission formalizes the following lower bounds for WL:

      • Time. For every fixed k≥3k \geq 3k≥3 and ε>0\varepsilon > 0ε>0, no deterministic multitape Turing machine decides whether kkk-WL distinguishes two given colored graphs in time O(nk−1−ε)O(n^{k-1-\varepsilon})O(nk−1−ε), where nnn is the length of the binary encoding of the input pair. This almost matches the classical upper bound of O(nk+1log⁡n)O(n^{k+1} \log n)O(nk+1logn). When kkk is part of the input, the problem is EXPTIME\mathsf{EXPTIME}EXPTIME-hard under polynomial-time many-one reductions, and XP\mathsf{XP}XP-hard under fpt-reductions when parameterized by kkk; moreover, no deterministic multitape Turing machine decides it in time O(2εN1/5)O(2^{\varepsilon N^{1/5}})O(2εN1/5) for some ε>0\varepsilon > 0ε>0, where NNN is the length of the encoded instance.
      • Iteration number. On nnn-vertex graphs, the iteration number of kkk-WL is Ωk(nk−1)\Omega_k(n^{k-1})Ωk​(nk−1), matching the upper bound of Döring and Neuen.
      • Witness size. There are pairs of nnn-vertex graphs distinguished by kkk-WL for which every graph FFF of treewidth at most kkk with hom⁡(F,G0)≠hom⁡(F,G1)\hom(F, G_0) \neq \hom(F, G_1)hom(F,G0​)=hom(F,G1​) has 2Ωk(nk−1)2^{\Omega_k(n^{k-1})}2Ωk​(nk−1) vertices. This is complemented by an upper bound of 2Ok(nk−1log⁡n)2^{O_k(n^{k-1} \log n)}2Ok​(nk−1logn), also stated for uncolored graphs in the language of homomorphism indistinguishability.

      All results are obtained via a unified framework. Implicit parity systems are succinctly represented systems of linear equations over F2\mathbb F_2F2​. For each implicit parity system with kkk coordinate blocks, the matrix compiler constructs a pair of graphs on which the bijective (k+1)(k+1)(k+1)-pebble game, and hence kkk-WL, exactly simulates unit propagation in the system. Deterministic computations are encoded into such systems by a recursive simulation due to Koucký, in which the calls of one recursion depth share their locations and the call paths are packed into the coordinate blocks; the reductions are carried out by explicit multitape Turing machines.

      Everything is proved, including the pebble game and homomorphism characterizations of kkk-WL, the stabilization bound of Döring and Neuen, the deterministic time hierarchy theorem (for polynomial bounds, and for the exponential bounds 2n2^n2n versus 2n/42^{n/4}2n/4), and the translations from the archive's single-tape and multi-stack machine models used for EXPTIME\mathsf{EXPTIME}EXPTIME and many-one reductions. Membership of the problem in EXPTIME\mathsf{EXPTIME}EXPTIME and XP\mathsf{XP}XP is not formalized. The class XP\mathsf{XP}XP and fpt-reductions are defined here with deterministic multitape Turing machines.
